topic:
The sharp finite-population price of fractional causal variance bounds. For each integer N>=2 take three multisets x_a=(x_a1,...,x_aN) in [0,1]^N, repeats permitted. Fixed contrast c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2). Put F_a=N^-1 sum_i delta_x_ai. V_rel(x)=inf over all probability couplings pi with marginals(F1,F2,F3) of E_pi[(sum_a c_a Y_a)^2]. V_int(x)=min over permutations sigma2,sigma3 of N^-1 sum_i(c1 x_1i+c2 x_2,sigma2(i)+c3 x_3,sigma3(i))^2. Define Delta_N=sup_x[V_int(x)-V_rel(x)]. Population marginal means are fixed, so the identical gap holds for contrast variances. For N>=3, under complete random assignment with fixed positive arm sizes n1+n2+n3=N, the sharp estimator-variance upper bound based on the known marginals differs between fractional and realizable completions by (V_int-V_rel)/(N-1). No claim that all full marginals are observed in one experiment. Determine the sharp asymptotic order of Delta_N, with any necessary arithmetic subsequences explicitly resolved: derive an explicit rate sequence r_N and universal constants 0<a<=b<infinity such that a r_N<=Delta_N<=b r_N for all sufficiently large N (or exact zero exceptional N classified). Prove the upper bound by a deterministic algorithm, polynomial in N and rational-input bit length, that takes empirical marginals and an optimal rational fractional coupling and outputs N-row permutations with cost at most V_rel+b r_N. Prove the matching lower bound over the SAME three-arm scalar [0,1] class by explicit families. The exponent/log factors and proof mechanics are answer-open; no unverified rate is assumed. Translate the guarantee into computable two-sided certificates for the marginal-information sharp randomization variance, and provide a consistent plug-in estimator of its endpoints under complete randomization, deriving sampling error from the empirical marginal distributions. A generic finite LP or an arbitrary vanishing rate is insufficient. Grounding: Gao-Ge-Qian (AISTATS2025), Brennan et al. (ICML2025), Haus (2015), and Puccetti-Wang (2015); the new object is same-empirical-marginal fractional-versus-N-row squared-cost loss, not quantile-discretization error, a generic integer program, or ordinary bottleneck mixability. Consumer: three-arm contrast comparisons within published multi-arm trials such as ACTG175 (Hammer et al.1996). PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The informal draft derives ordered support-slope intervals from fractional LP duality, builds nested dyadic partitions, freezes integer masses from successive basic feasible tables, and repairs each marginal hierarchically. Its quadratic slack accounting gives a candidate universal upper bound 3456/N. An exactly certified four-row obstruction, padded with isolated dummy rows, gives 1/(46080N) for every N at least four. Thus the supported answer is a sharp 1/N rate within the original answer-open coordinates. Thirty-six rational implementation checks passed, using numerical bases only as proposals followed by exact rational verification. Repeated atoms, dyadic boundary contacts, replication parity, and the two-row case were checked; arbitrarily tiny rational gaps are covered by the bit-length argument rather than a floating-point LP experiment. The variance certificates concern the sharp upper endpoint, with sampling uncertainty separately retained.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the slope-interval bound, residual-to-repair accounting, and polynomial rational vertex extraction; no remaining structural mathematical gap was identified, but standard LP, tree-matching, quantile/gluing and sampling steps remain compressed.
EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the three load-bearing inequalities on exact optimal supports with ties and boundary contacts; stop this route on a counterexample, or on a verified same-marginal sharp-rounding prior-art collision.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/mill/scratch/mill-w10/round1040_presolve_strongest.md. PRACTICAL LIMITATION: The useful numerical certificate is the actual primal-dual width. The loose universal 3456/N bound may be uninformative at ordinary trial sizes, and the sampling uncertainty is larger than the deterministic rounding term asymptotically.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp asymptotic order of the worst-case same-empirical-marginal fractional-versus-N-row loss for the three-arm contrast (1/4,1/4,-1/2), including arithmetic exceptions, a rational polynomial-time rounding algorithm, and matching explicit lower-bound families.

source_refs.claim: After exhibiting non-Monge optimal empirical multi-marginal quadratic transports, the paper identifies quantitative Monge-approximation error as future work.
source_refs.author: Pedram Emami and Brendan Pass

source_refs.claim: Discrete joint mixability is strongly NP-complete for fixed column count; its PTAS concerns a bottleneck objective, not additive squared-cost rounding.
source_refs.author: Utz-Uwe Haus

source_refs.claim: Causal partial identification with K potential-outcome marginals is formulated as fractional multi-marginal optimal transport without imposing N-row realizability.
source_refs.author: Zijun Gao, Shu Ge, and Jian Qian

source_refs.excerpt: No same-size integrality assertion for \(K>2\), and no cross-history assertion
Its polynomial support reduction is existential rather than algorithmic.
discrepancy rounding is reserved for additional product-law, deterministic-law, or prescribed-support restrictions

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two-marginal Birkhoff integrality mechanism disappears for three marginals. The closest prior CausalSmith transport result realizes a rational optimum only after denominator-dependent replication and explicitly makes no same-size K>2 claim, while the commitment-design proposal reduces support only existentially. Haus addresses exact mixability and bottleneck approximation rather than uniform additive loss for this bounded rank-one quadratic cost; Emami and Pass use a different quadratic orientation; and Gao, Ge, and Qian estimate the fractional target without rounding it into one N-unit science table. The missing proof must round an exact optimal support while preserving three marginal count vectors, control the cost of nonlocal repairs, and remain polynomial in rational-input bit length despite arbitrarily small positive masses, ties, and boundary contacts.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give an explicit rate r_N and universal constants 0<a<=b<infinity with a r_N<=Delta_N<=b r_N for all sufficiently large N, classify exceptional N, construct in bit-polynomial time two permutations of cost at most V_rel+b r_N from an optimal rational coupling, and exhibit rational three-arm scalar instances attaining a r_N.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing moves directly from the tractable Kantorovich relaxation to empirical Monge implementability and quantitative approximation error.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Empirical multi-marginal transport is naturally fractional -> an N-row finite population requires a Monge plan -> Monge optimality can fail -> quantify the exact additive price in the scalar causal-variance geometry

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the encoding of column permutations as fixed-dimensional assignment and its approximation decomposition, replacing bottleneck control by additive control of the mean squared row contrast.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems form common rows from equal-weight marginal columns; the desired theorem must exploit the special rank-one squared cost beyond generic assignment hardness.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the empirical multi-marginal-transport plug-in estimator and quadratic-cost stability proof, then append the new deterministic realization-error certificate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its fractional estimand is exactly V_rel, so its sampling analysis supplies the estimation rung once same-N rounding is controlled.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct computable two-sided certificates for the sharp finite-population randomization-variance upper endpoint of a three-arm contrast, separating armwise sampling uncertainty from the deterministic fractional-to-N-row realization loss.

source_refs.claim: For two-arm complete randomization, the paper gives consistent estimators of sharp variance bounds and asymptotically narrow conservative Wald intervals.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Donald P. Green, and Donald K. K. Lee

source_refs.claim: The paper proves plug-in convergence results for fractional multi-marginal quadratic causal bounds but does not incorporate finite-population row realizability.
source_refs.author: Zijun Gao, Shu Ge, and Jian Qian

source_refs.author: Jennifer Brennan, Sébastien Lahaie, Adel Javanmard, Nick Doudchenko, and Jean Pouget-Abadie

source_refs.excerpt: State and prove an explicit history-uniform endpoint error bound in terms of the minimum arm count, B_n
State an explicit conditional sampling-without-replacement transport stability lemma
adding a finite-pilot uniform deviation bound for the robust value or an implementable confidence rule

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two-arm sharp-bound construction uses bivariate extremal couplings, where discrete uniform couplings are permutation-realizable. With three arms, the fractional endpoint need not correspond to any N-unit potential-outcome table, while a realizable endpoint is a data-dependent combinatorial optimum near a possibly nonsmooth LP value. Complete randomization also produces dependent sampling-without-replacement empirical marginals, and tied atoms or changing optimal faces can invalidate a smooth delta-method argument. The missing result must propagate marginal empirical-process error through the transport endpoint and its rounding certificate without counting the deterministic realization loss twice.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would provide data-computable lower and upper certificates whose deterministic width equals a certified fractional-to-integral loss divided by N-1, together with consistent plug-in endpoint estimators and either a finite-population limit law or a uniform coverage bound valid at repeated atoms and nonunique optimal couplings.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation proceeds from unidentified finite-population covariance to sharp marginal-information variance bounds and usable conservative confidence intervals.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Randomization identifies arm means but not cross-world dependence -> estimator variance depends on that missing dependence -> marginal-compatible sharp bounds improve Neyman inference -> add a three-arm realizability band and separately quantified sampling uncertainty

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the plug-in multi-marginal-transport estimator and quadratic-cost stability analysis to armwise empirical marginal laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The fractional certificate endpoint is the same quadratic transport functional, leaving the design-based sampling law and integer band as the new layers.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the sharp-bound plug-in construction and conservative-Wald argument, replacing bivariate Hoeffding couplings by a three-marginal fractional endpoint plus a certified realization remainder.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the precise inferential object sought, but only in the two-arm zero-integrality-loss case.

method_exemplars.technique: Use finite-population combinatorial central limit theorems for multiple treatment levels to derive the assignment-randomization limit law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its asymptotics preserve fixed potential outcomes and assignment as the sole randomness source.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize, for given three bounded scalar empirical marginals and contrast (1/4,1/4,-1/2), exactly when a fractional optimum is realizable by N common rows and provide a verifiable zero-gap certificate.

source_refs.claim: The review states that characterization of attainable sums under fixed marginals remains open in dimension at least two and organizes joint mixability through deterministic rearrangements.
source_refs.author: Giovanni Puccetti and Ruodu Wang

source_refs.claim: The paper proves hardness of recognizing general discrete joint mixability but also identifies tractable special cases, leaving cost-specific characterizations unresolved.
source_refs.author: Utz-Uwe Haus

open_problems.why_unsolved: General joint-mixability characterizations are incomplete and generic recognition is hard, but those facts do not decide the restricted three-column scalar problem with a fixed signed quadratic contrast. The familiar one-dimensional monotone Monge conclusion concerns an attractive cost orientation, whereas squared signed-sum minimization is a negative-dependence problem. Repeated atoms and dual ties prevent a criterion based only on strict order statistics; exact equality instead requires connecting the fractional LP's dual-tight support hypergraph to an integral perfect N-row decomposition.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give a necessary-and-sufficient condition in terms of empirical supports and an optimal dual-tight hypergraph, or an equivalent arithmetic object, that decides V_int=V_rel and outputs either realizing permutations or a positive rational separation certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames negative dependence through attainable sums and rearrangements, the natural language for separating fractional constant-sum couplings from row-realizable ones.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Marginals leave dependence unidentified -> extremal negative dependence minimizes dispersion of a sum -> deterministic rearrangements encode realizable dependence -> characterize exactly when the fractional optimum is row-realizable

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the matrix joint-mixability and multipartite-assignment encoding, then use the fixed contrast and scalar ordering to derive a specialized feasibility certificate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Zero gap is precisely the existence of an optimal common-row rearrangement, but the desired certificate must be sharper than generic hardness results.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its comparison of fractional extreme plans with Monge plans and its boundary-case arguments for Monge existence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It isolates exact empirical Monge existence as a structural property of the optimal transport plan.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply empirical transport stability to determine when a population or empirical zero-gap condition can be consistently certified from armwise samples.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once exact realizability is characterized, the causal use case requires learning its endpoint from estimated marginal laws.

open_problems.open_problem: For every fixed K>=4, bounded scalar marginals, and zero-sum contrast c, determine the optimal dependence on N, K, and c of the worst additive fractional-versus-N-row quadratic contrast loss, including its exact-zero regimes.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The arbitrary-K causal literature supplies the fractional target, while assignment results supply generic hardness or bottleneck approximation; neither gives a same-marginal additive theorem for rank-one squared contrast costs. The prior proposals likewise use denominator-clearing replication or leave universal rates and global balance open. A three-arm repair proof does not extend formally: residual mass lies in a K-partite support hypergraph, repairing one marginal can disturb several previously repaired marginals, and the attainable constant may depend on contrast sparsity or norms. The first proof step that must change is the three-table support decomposition, which must become a K-marginal discrepancy or flow decomposition preserving the original row count.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would characterize a minimax rate r_{N,K,c}, prove matching bounds uniformly over K bounded empirical marginals, classify exact-zero regimes, and give an exact-arithmetic rounding procedure polynomial in N for each fixed K with explicit dependence on the geometry of c.

writing_exemplar.why: Its arbitrary-K missing-potential-outcome formulation supplies the clean destination language and makes finite-population realizability the remaining boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Multiple potential outcomes are never jointly observed -> K-marginal transport gives the fractional sharp target -> empirical estimation is available -> finite-population use requires a K-way same-row approximation theorem

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the fixed-column multidimensional-assignment formulation and approximation decomposition to additive average squared-contrast loss.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest algorithmic treatment of common-row rearrangements with a fixed but arbitrary number of marginal columns.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over arbitrary-K quadratic transport plug-in estimation and append the new K-dependent deterministic rounding remainder.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already controls statistical estimation of the exact fractional object for arbitrary K.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the worst-case-copula integer-program formulation and asymptotic-validity argument as a benchmark for an explicit fixed-K rounding certificate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its broad linear and quadratic estimator class shows how a dependence completion enters causal inference while exposing the lack of an analytic additive guarantee.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the finite-N fractional-versus-realizable gap for the covariance image of several three-arm contrasts when one common N-row potential-outcome schedule must certify every direction simultaneously.

source_refs.excerpt: non-representability by one conservative quadratic covariance envelope
The covariance-set image is sharp conditional on the full assignment-cell marginal table \(f\).
Scoped out of v1: graph families beyond two-block, the fixed-treatment-count design class

open_problems.why_unsolved: A scalar rounding theorem may choose a different N-row completion for every contrast, so it does not characterize covariance matrices jointly realizable by one finite population. The saturation proposal records that directionwise-sharp variances need not be represented by one conservative quadratic covariance envelope, while the ±1 design proposal identifies a related relaxation-versus-implementability boundary but excludes fixed treatment counts. The scalar support argument is therefore insufficient: a covariance-image result needs one schedule controlling all quadratic forms simultaneously, or a support-function approximation uniform over the requested contrast set.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give a Hausdorff or uniform support-function rate between the fractional covariance image and the covariance image generated by N-row schedules, a polynomial simultaneous-rounding algorithm, and a matching family showing the optimal dependence on N and the number or geometry of contrasts.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing treats variance bounds across designs and quadratic directions as objects to compare and optimize, motivating a joint covariance certificate rather than incompatible scalar endpoints.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Complex experiments require valid covariance bounds -> optimizing one quadratic direction can be inadequate for another -> several reported contrasts need one jointly realizable certificate -> quantify the fractional-to-finite-population covariance-image loss

method_exemplars.technique: Represent each contrast-specific support function of the fractional covariance image as a quadratic multi-marginal transport problem and seek uniform control over directions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniformizing these support functions is the natural bridge from scalar transport endpoints to a covariance-body characterization.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt covariance-order and admissibility arguments for quadratic variance bounds under a fixed randomization design.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is a jointly valid covariance certificate whose support functions control every reported causal contrast.

literature_map:
Emami and Pass (2024, arXiv:2401.12417) isolate empirical Monge-versus-Kantorovich optimality and call for rigorous quantification of Monge approximation error.
Their quadratic barycenter orientation is equivalent to maximizing a squared sum, so its one-dimensional Monge result does not settle minimization of this mixed-sign squared contrast.
Gao, Ge, and Qian (AISTATS 2025, arXiv:2406.07868) identify causal partial-identification sets through K-marginal transport and establish plug-in rates for quadratic costs.
Their target is fractional and does not require a coupling to be an N-row potential-outcome schedule with the same empirical marginals.
Brennan et al. (ICML 2025, arXiv:2410.21464) compute worst-case causal copulas by integer programming and distinguish finite-population design uncertainty from sampling uncertainty.
Their results do not provide an explicit same-marginal additive rounding rate or rational constructive certificate.
Haus (Operations Research Letters 2015, arXiv:1407.6475) proves strong NP-completeness of discrete joint mixability for fixed column count and develops bottleneck approximation results.
Haus's hardness rules out reliance on generic exact permutation optimization but leaves open uniform additive approximation for bounded rank-one squared costs.
Puccetti and Wang (Statistical Science 2015, arXiv:1512.03232) organize extremal negative dependence through rearrangements and identify attainable-sum characterization as an open area.
Their related discretization work concerns approximating continuous marginal problems, not fractional-versus-permutation loss for the same empirical marginals.
Aronow, Green, and Lee (Annals of Statistics 2014, arXiv:1405.6555) give sharp two-arm finite-population variance bounds and consistent endpoint estimators using bivariate extremal couplings.
Li and Ding (JASA 2017, arXiv:1610.04821) provide assignment-based finite-population central limit theorems for multiple treatment levels.
Hammer et al. (NEJM 1996, DOI 10.1056/NEJM199610103351501) report the 2,467-participant, four-regimen ACTG 175 trial, a concrete multi-arm contrast use case.
Targeted searches found no prior theorem combining a same-empirical-marginal additive Monge-versus-fractional rate, arithmetic exception classification, matching scalar lower bounds, and a bit-polynomial rounding algorithm.
